home.empty-text: A project remembers a database file, and its password if you like, so it opens again in one click.
home.not-database: {{name}} points at a file that is not a DaruDB database. Edit the project to choose another one.
home.open-elsewhere: {{name}} is open in another window, which is now in front.
home.step-create: Create a project and give it a name.
home.step-file: Choose the database file it opens. Any extension works.
home.step-open: Open the project to browse its collections and edit its objects.
home.welcome-text: Browse, edit and query the files of DaruDB, the embedded database for Rust, Node.js, Python and Dart.

project-dialog.copy-replaced: The working copy the app made for this project is deleted when you save.
project-dialog.delete-copy-text: The project is removed from the list, along with the working copy the app made. The original file stays where it is.
project-dialog.delete-text: The project is removed from the list. The database file stays where it is.
project-dialog.file-error: This file could not be read: {{message}}
project-dialog.file-missing: There is no file at this path any more. Choose another one.
project-dialog.file-ok: A DaruDB database, in format version {{version}}.
project-dialog.file-required: Choose the database file the project opens.
project-dialog.file-upgrade: It is in an older format version. You will be asked how to open it.
project-dialog.name: Project name
project-dialog.no-keystore: This system has no keystore to keep a password in, so you will be asked for it each time.
project-dialog.not-database: This file is not a DaruDB database. Choose another one.
project-dialog.not-encrypted: This file is not encrypted, so it needs no password.
project-dialog.password-hint: Kept encrypted by your system. Leave it empty to be asked each time.
project-dialog.password-kept: A password is saved. Type another one to replace it.
project-dialog.save-failed: The project could not be saved: {{message}}
project-dialog.wrong-password: This password does not open the file.

open-dialog.damaged-text: The file did not open, because part of it is damaged. A rescue copies what can still be read into a new file, and leaves this one as it is.
open-dialog.missing-text: There is nothing at {{path}} any more. The file may have been moved, renamed or deleted.
open-dialog.password-text: The file of {{name}} is encrypted. Type its password to open it.
open-dialog.password-wrong: This password does not open the file.
open-dialog.password-wrong-saved: The saved password no longer opens the file. Type the current one.
open-dialog.upgrade-copy-text: The app copies the file into its own folder and raises the copy. The original stays readable by older versions.
open-dialog.upgrade-original-text: The file itself is raised. Programs on an older version of DaruDB can no longer open it.
open-dialog.upgrade-text: The file of {{name}} is in format version {{from}}. This app opens files in format version {{to}}.

settings.edit-immediate-text: Each edit is written to the file as soon as you make it.
settings.edit-submit-text: Edits wait until you submit them from the toolbar, and can be discarded until then.
settings.restore: Restore the last workspace when the app starts
settings.restore-text: Opens the windows, projects and tabs that were open when the app last quit.
settings.title: Settings

notices.missing: The notices are written when the app is built, and this run was started without them.
notices.text: DaruDB Studio is built with these open source packages, each under its own license.
notices.title: Third-Party Licenses

sidebar.no-schema-text: This file was written without a schema, so its objects cannot be read.
sidebar.title: Collections

toolbar.discard-text: The edits you have not submitted are dropped, and the file stays as it is.
toolbar.import-insert-text: Stops at a key the collection already has
toolbar.import-put-text: Replaces the object that has the same key
toolbar.import-title: Import objects from JSON or CSV

import-dialog.text: These records of {{path}} do not fit the collection. Fix them, and import the file again.
import-dialog.title: Nothing was imported

workspace.collection-gone: The file no longer has a collection called {{name}}.
workspace.empty-text: Choose a collection in the sidebar to see its objects.
workspace.filter-placeholder: Filter, such as age >= 18 AND city == "Seoul"
workspace.merge-left: Merge into the Group on the Left
workspace.no-objects: This collection has no objects yet.

grid.delete-held: They are deleted from the file when you submit your changes.
grid.delete-now: They are deleted from the file at once. This cannot be undone.

object-dialog.bytes-hint: Pairs of hex digits, such as 0a 1b 2c.
object-dialog.json-hint: JSON. Bytes are written as a string of hex digits.
object-dialog.key-assigned: The key is assigned when the object is inserted.
object-dialog.key-fixed: The key names the object, so it does not change.
object-dialog.too-long: This value has too many items for the form. Edit it as JSON.

query.not-run: Write a query and run it.
query.placeholder: age >= 18 SORT BY age DESC LIMIT 100
query.too-many: This query finds {{count}} objects, more than the {{limit}} a tab shows. Add a LIMIT to see them a page at a time.

tools.backup-encrypt: Encrypt the copy with a password of its own
tools.backup-text: Writes a copy of the file where you choose, under the same password. The copy holds no free space.
tools.check-ok: No problems. Checked {{pages}} pages and {{objects}} objects.
tools.check-rescue: A rescue copies what can still be read into a new file.
tools.check-text: Reads every page of the file and reports any damage it finds.
tools.compact-text: Moves the pages in use to the start of the file and gives the free space back to the disk.
tools.password-remembered: The password was changed, and the project remembers the new one.
tools.password-text: The file opens with the new password from now on, and no longer with the old one.
tools.rescue-closed: The file did not open again afterwards, so the project was closed.
tools.rescue-partial: Rescued what could be read into {{path}}. {{pages}} damaged pages were skipped, which lost {{objects}} objects and {{values}} values.
tools.rescue-text: Copies every object the file can still give into a new file, skipping the damaged pages, and adds the new file as a project. The file itself stays as it is.
tools.rescue-whole: Nothing was damaged. Every object is in {{path}}.

unload.text: The edits held for a submit are lost when the window closes.
unload.title: Close without submitting your changes?
